adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30 — NewSQLCommand always fails via stubbed TablesList and surfaces a misleading "error reading SQL command" BadRequest, masking that the backend was removed rather than the user's SQL being invalid.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior DuckDB-backed implementation and replaces it with a new `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` where `TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` all unconditionally return `errors.New("not implemented")`. In `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go`, `TablesList` now calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...)`, which will always error. In `pkg/expr/sql_command.go`, `Execute` now calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto(...)`, which will also always error. This makes SQL expression parsing/execution fail at runtime whenever these paths are reached; while the finding’s claim about the exact surfaced BadRequest message and `NewSQLCommand` isn’t directly shown in the diff, the underlying always-failing behavior due to stubs is verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:24 — SQL is still built with fmt.Sprintf and only single-quote doubling; escaping kept in place for a future engine is fragile (backslash/dialect escapes) and logs raw user SQL at error level.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList still constructs a SQL command via fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL) after only doubling single quotes (strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)), which is indeed a fragile/limited escaping approach if/when a real SQL engine executes it. However, in this diff NewInMemoryDB() returns a stub DB whose RunCommands returns "not implemented", so this is not a currently verifiable security/correctness defect. The claim that it "logs raw user SQL at error level" is not supported by the shown diff (the only visible raw SQL logging is at Debug level in SQLCommand.Execute).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12 — Unused DB.TablesList method duplicates package-level TablesList and is dead code alongside the stub.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `type DB` in `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` with a stub method `(*DB).TablesList` returning `not implemented`, while the existing behavior in `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` uses the package-level `TablesList(rawSQL string)` function and calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...)` (not `db.TablesList`). Within the shown changes there is no reference to `(*DB).TablesList`, and it duplicates the concept/name of the package-level `TablesList`, creating likely-dead/placeholder API surface and potential confusion, though it’s not a runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: go.work.sum:312 — go-duck and transitive deps are dropped from go.mod/go.sum but moved into go.work.sum, leaving inconsistent workspace checksums unrelated to the stated feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck` from `go.mod` and `go.sum`, but `go.work.sum` does not add `go-duck` (or its `duck` module) anywhere. The `go.work.sum` additions shown are for `github.com/JohnCGriffin/overflow`, `github.com/apache/thrift`, `github.com/klauspost/asmfmt`, and `github.com/minio/*`, not `go-duck`. So the finding’s claim that go-duck was “moved into go.work.sum” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:194 — enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path, so SQL expression queries get rejected even with the sqlExpressions feature flag enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go the newly added enableSqlExpressions() returns false on all paths: it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` but then `if enabled { return false }` and finally `return false`. ReadQuery now rejects QueryTypeSQL when `!enabled`, so SQL expression queries will always error even if the feature flag is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:131 — The SQL query type now returns an untyped "not implemented" error instead of a structured errutil/feature-disabled response, which changes the error contract for API callers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `QueryTypeSQL` now short-circuits with `return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` (pkg/expr/reader.go). However, the claim that this replaces a previously structured `errutil`/feature-disabled error response (and thus changes an established API error contract) is not verifiable from the provided diff, since the prior behavior/error type isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12 — The stub DB.TablesList/RunCommands always error, so sql.TablesList fails and NewSQLCommand returns sql-invalid-sql 400 for every valid SQL expression.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/db.go, DB.RunCommands and DB.QueryFramesInto unconditionally return "not implemented" errors. pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:TablesList now constructs this DB via NewInMemoryDB() and then calls duckDB.RunCommands(...), so TablesList will always error for any input SQL. (The finding’s additional claim about NewSQLCommand returning a specific 400 error isn’t verifiable from this diff, and reader.go currently blocks SQL expressions anyway, but the underlying always-failing DB/ TablesList behavior is a real defect if that codepath is used.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:20 — QueryFramesInto is a stub that always errors, so every SQLCommand.Execute response carries an error instead of frames, breaking the response shape for consumers.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/db.go, DB.QueryFramesInto unconditionally returns errors.New("not implemented"). The diff also changes pkg/expr/sql_command.go to construct sql.NewInMemoryDB() and call db.QueryFramesInto(...), so any execution reaching SQLCommand.Execute will always hit this stub and return an error instead of producing frames (previously it used duck.NewInMemoryDB()).

adjudication_records.issue_text: go.mod:145 — Removing the go-duck dependency without a working replacement silently drops the SQL expressions capability for all existing consumers (dashboards/alert rules using type=sql).

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck` dependency and replaces it with a new `pkg/expr/sql` package whose DB methods (`RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`, `TablesList`) all return `errors.New("not implemented")` (pkg/expr/sql/db.go). Additionally, SQL query reading is now gated by `enableSqlExpressions(h)` which currently returns `false` unconditionally (pkg/expr/reader.go), causing `QueryTypeSQL` to immediately error (`return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`). This breaks existing SQL expressions (dashboards/alert rules using type=sql) rather than providing a working replacement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:104 — The execution error from the stub DB goes to consumers as a raw "not implemented" string with no public message or status mapping.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` introduces an in-memory `DB` whose methods (including `QueryFramesInto`) return `errors.New("not implemented")`. `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` now calls `db.QueryFramesInto(...)` and, on error, assigns it directly to `rsp.Error` without wrapping/mapping (`rsp.Error = err`). So if this path is executed, consumers will indeed see the raw stub error string. However, the diff does not prove a required public/status error mapping contract here (and `ReadQuery` also blocks SQL expressions via a feature check), so it's better framed as an incomplete implementation/UX/API concern rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:194 — enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path (and negates the flag), so SQL expressions are always rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false both in the `if enabled { return false }` branch and the final `return false`, so it can never return true. In ReadQuery's QueryTypeSQL case, this causes SQL expressions to always be rejected (`if !enabled { return ..., fmt.Errorf(...) }`) even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:131 — The error for a disabled feature flag says "not implemented", which misreports the cause and masks the always-false toggle bug.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go the new gating logic for QueryTypeSQL is broken: enableSqlExpressions() always returns false (it returns false both when the flag is enabled and when it is not). As a result SQL queries will always error. The returned error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" also misstates the actual cause (feature disabled / toggle logic bug), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:16 — RunCommands/QueryFramesInto are stubs that always return "not implemented" after go-duck was removed, so every SQL expression parse and execution fails.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the go-duck dependency and introduces pkg/expr/sql/db.go where RunCommands and QueryFramesInto always return errors.New("not implemented"). These methods are directly used by SQL parsing/execution paths shown in the diff: TablesList() in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go now calls NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...), which will always error, and SQLCommand.Execute in pkg/expr/sql_command.go now calls sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto(...), which will always error. Additionally, ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery adds a gate that returns an error for QueryTypeSQL when enableSqlExpressions(h) is false, and enableSqlExpressions currently returns false unconditionally, guaranteeing failure for SQL queries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23 — TablesList now always errors via the stub DB, so SQLCommand construction returns BadRequest "invalid sql" for valid queries (misleading error propagation).

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now instantiates duckDB := NewInMemoryDB(). The new implementation in pkg/expr/sql/db.go returns an empty *DB whose methods (RunCommands, TablesList, QueryFramesInto, etc.) all return errors.New("not implemented"). Therefore TablesList’s call to duckDB.RunCommands(...) will always error, breaking SQL table parsing for any valid SQL input. The added claim about SQLCommand returning a BadRequest "invalid sql" isn’t shown in this diff, but the underlying behavior regression (TablesList always failing) is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:43 — tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without a length check, so an empty JSON array would panic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff for pkg/expr/sql/parser.go only shows an import removal and changing `duck.NewInMemoryDB()` to `NewInMemoryDB()`. It does not show a `tablesFromAST` function or any `ast[0]` indexing, so the claimed panic on empty JSON array cannot be verified from the provided diff and appears unrelated to the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:194 — enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path so SQL expressions are always rejected, and no reader test covers flag-on vs flag-off behavior to catch it.

adjudication.rationale:
In pkg/expr/reader.go the new enableSqlExpressions() helper returns false on all code paths:

```
enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)
if enabled { return false }
return false
```

ReadQuery() uses this to gate QueryTypeSQL and returns an error when !enabled, so SQL expressions will always be rejected regardless of the feature flag value. The comment about missing tests is not verifiable from this diff, but the always-false gating logic is a concrete behavioral defect shown in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:129 — New feature-flag gate on QueryTypeSQL adds a behavioral error path with no accompanying test in the change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new feature-flag gate in `pkg/expr/reader.go` under `case QueryTypeSQL` that can return early with `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` before parsing/handling SQL expressions. No test files are added/updated in this PR diff to cover this new conditional error path, so the review point about missing accompanying test is grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12 — New DB type replaces go-duck with stubs that always return "not implemented" and has zero tests asserting real query behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the go-duck dependency and introduces a new `pkg/expr/sql.DB` whose methods (`TablesList`, `RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`) always return `errors.New("not implemented")`. These stubs are immediately used: `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` now calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands(...)`, which will always error, and `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` now calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto(...)`, which will always error. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable behavior break (SQL paths cannot function). The claim about “zero tests” is plausible because no tests are added in the diff, but the core issue is the introduced always-failing implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23 — TablesList now always errors via the stub DB, a regression that no parser test verifies (no pkg/expr/sql tests exist).

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now constructs duckDB := NewInMemoryDB() instead of duck.NewInMemoryDB(). The new pkg/expr/sql/db.go implementation is a stub: RunCommands (and other methods) always return `errors.New("not implemented")`. Since TablesList immediately calls `duckDB.RunCommands(...)`, it will now always error at runtime, which is a clear functional regression introduced by this diff. The additional claim about missing tests can’t be verified from the diff alone, but the always-error behavior is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96 — SQLCommand.Execute now always fails via stub QueryFramesInto, and no sql_command test exercises Execute end-to-end to detect the regression.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the previous DuckDB-backed implementation (`duck.NewInMemoryDB()`) with `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go`, and the new `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` implementation is a stub: `(*DB).QueryFramesInto(...)` unconditionally returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. Therefore `SQLCommand.Execute` will always return an error at runtime when reached. The claim about lack of an end-to-end test is not verifiable from this diff alone, but the always-failing behavior is directly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:24 — NewInMemoryDB lacks edge-case tests (empty frames, quoted SQL, invalid SQL) for the advertised analytics framework.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` with `NewInMemoryDB()` returning an empty `*DB`, but all DB methods (`TablesList`, `RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`) currently return `errors.New("not implemented")`. The finding claims missing edge-case tests (empty frames, quoted SQL, invalid SQL) for an “advertised analytics framework,” but the diff shows no implemented behavior to test and no mention of such a framework. From the diff alone, the absence of specific edge-case tests is not a verifiable, actionable issue tied to this stub implementation.
